criteria.note: src/shared/domain/space.ts defines typed contracts for policy (SpacePolicy), observations (MetricObservation), baselines (BudgetBaseline/CohortBaseline and BaselineRef), grades (SpaceGrade, ComponentGrade, GradeCap) and evidence (EvidenceRef). They cover units (METRIC_UNITS, with time in ms), scope (a level plus a stable id), source kind/ref (human is separate from agent_report), observed/estimated/missing states, and the new stable-id prefixes mo/bl/as in src/core/ids.ts. The strict zod schemas in src/core/space/schemas.ts enforce: null exactly when missing, unit equals the catalog unit, a human rating needs a human source, id prefixes, scope id of the scope's level, and baseline unit matches its resource. The compile-time Same<> asserts are well-formed. Fixtures under src/core/space/fixtures are checked in: policy, 10 observations covering all three states plus an inherited sprint rating, 5 baselines, and 4 examples. I reran node_modules/.bin/tsx scratch/dm-169-demo.ts: the c1 section prints 25 PASS, and all fixtures parse plus 12 rejection cases.

docs/space-grading.md specifies a deterministic 0–100 normalization per component, 1/7 base weights, A≥90/B≥80/C≥70/D≥60/F<60, rounding once to 2 dp followed by an exact integer weighted mean, display truncation after the letter is fixed, and worked complete, sparse, unverified and failure examples. rubric.ts implements this: toUnits/weightedUnits use floor((2n+p)/2p) for round-half-up, and letterFor/displayOf follow the rules. I checked the arithmetic by hand: complete 585/7 → 83.57 B, shown "83.5"; sparse 255/4 → 63.75 D; failure 500/6 → 83.33, capped to 59.99 F. In the demo's c2 section all 18 lines PASS: the boundary letters at 90/89.99/…/59.99, the re-graded examples deep-equal the checked-in expected grades, and 89.9857 is stored as 89.99 (B) and shown as "89.9".

In statusOf/normalizePerformance, an empty, pending or missing required verification gives ungraded with required_verification_missing and a null score, letter and display. A failed required item sets P to 0 and adds a mandatory_failure cap at 59.99 with its evidence, so the letter is F. Coverage below 4 weight units gives insufficient_coverage. Missing components carry effectiveWeight 0 and the present ones are renormalized, with no imputation. Every grade carries coverage (present/total units, missing and estimated lists). The demo's c3 section prints 12 PASS. I also probed it myself with tsx -e: a failure with every other component missing → provisional F 0 at coverage 1/7 (rule 1 as documented); a failure plus a pending check → provisional F 59.99; an estimated time input → provisional; the unverified example → ungraded with all effective weights 0 and coverage reported.

In baselines.ts selectBaseline, a candidate is eligible only if it has the same resource and unit, a positive value and a matching identity (a budget for this exact subject, or a cohort with the same workType/size/risk). A cohort also needs sampleSize ≥ policy.minCohortSampleSize (5), and frozenAt and the cohort windowEnd must both be ≤ dispatchedAt; NaN fails closed. Any eligible budget beats a cohort. When nothing is eligible, normalizeResource returns the component as missing with the reason, never 100. The demo's c4 section prints 13 PASS. With the edited v2 budget (2M, frozen after dispatch) present, the sparse grade is identical to the v1-only grade (tokens 80, pinned v1). With only v2, tokens are missing (frozen_after_dispatch) and the grade is ungraded.

Minor items that are not reasons to reject:

2. `npm run deadcode` will flag the new exports until DM-171..176 add producers (already filed).
3. A duplicate id or an unresolved carry-forward rejects a whole run file, and a carry-forward run is rejected in turn when its original's run is rejected (already filed).
4. A carry-forward ticket can still have usage recorded at ticket scope with no attempt, and it is counted.
5. The DM-169 fixtures use `ss_` ids as source refs, which the ledger now refuses (filed).

reasons:
c3 and correctness, `observationPlanIssue` in src/core/repo/importer.ts. An observation with no attempt is checked against the plan the run is on now (`record.revisionId`). `attribute` in src/core/services/observations.ts checked it against the run's plan at the time it was recorded. `adoptRevision` (src/core/services/adoption.ts) changes `runs.revision_id` and is allowed to move tickets to later sprints (`ticketsMovedLater`) or drop tickets and sprints. Reproduced from the worktree with the harness:
1. On makeBundle([[1,2,3],[4]]), record a ticket-scope token_usage observation for tid(3) with no attempt; the service fills in sprint 1.
2. A clone imports the run cleanly.
3. pauseRun, then seedRevision with makeBundle([[1,2],[3,4]]) plus its snapshot outbox entry, then adoptRevision and flush.
4. A new clone's reconcileRepository now rejects `history/<run>/run.json` with "Observation mo_…01: Ticket tk_…zb is in sprint sp_…yj, not sp_…yh."

The run's attempts, reports, checkpoints and observations therefore never reach any clone. Before this patch, the same run history imported fine.

Fix: pin the plan revision the attribution was checked against on the entry, for example a `revisionId` in `ledgerEntry`, the payload hash and a new column. Then check against that revision in both `attribute` and `observationPlanIssue`. Alternatively, accept an attribution that is valid in a revision the run actually executed.

Add a scratch/DM-170 demo that adopts a revision moving a ticket (and one dropping a sprint) and shows a clone still imports the run with its observations.

c2, `localDataViolation` in src/core/space/ledger.ts, plus `resolveEntry` in src/core/services/observations.ts and `observationIssue` in src/core/repo/portable.ts. `observation.source.ref` is only checked for the stable-id pattern, so unknown references are accepted and exported. Fix:
- Refuse refs whose prefix is not in ID_PREFIXES.
- For records the ledger can resolve, require the ref to exist and to belong to the observation's own run or epic. Those are this run's attempts, reports, checkpoints, row checks and observations, and the plan's revision, tickets and sprints.
- Apply the same rule in the run-history check, so imports and the service agree.
- Add these cases to scratch/DM-170/c2-idempotency-validation.ts.

Red-team: I ran a reviewer subagent (WorkerDM170.LedgerRedTeam) twice against my diff, with probe scripts.

Fixed after the first pass:
- Another run's claim tokens and grant tokens got through. Both are now refused, on the service side and on import.
- Disguised absolute paths got through: backticks, file URLs, comma- or bracket-led paths, /srv, $HOME.
- The importer accepted rehashed entries the service would refuse: a human source with an agent actor, a ticket outside the plan, the wrong sprint, a dangling carriedFrom, a path in the actor label.
- Two run files in one import could silently claim the same observation id.
- A long session label blocked the export permanently. It is now clipped, or replaced by the role.
- Line separators and control characters made the per-run cap unsafe by size. They are refused and the cap was lowered to 2,000; the worst case is measured at 2,610 B per entry, 5.2 MB per run.
- recordObservations did not check the branch, and listObservations did not check the read capability.

Fixed after the second pass:
- ~user paths, backslash-rooted paths, %APPDATA% paths and drive letters after an underscore got through.
- Lone surrogates were accepted.
- The import message for an unresolved carry-forward was unclear.

What held up: idempotency and conflicts, the append-only trigger, BEGIN IMMEDIATE atomicity, foreign keys during import and epic deletion, legacy byte and hash stability, and outbox atomicity with recovery.

Rejected or left open on purpose:
- The payload hash is unkeyed. Anyone who can edit tracked files can forge provenance that passes every rule. This is a design limit, not something this ticket can fix.
- A bare claim secret of another run without its `at_` prefix, or a token split with zero-width characters, cannot be told from an ordinary label.
- When the same observation id appears in two run files in one import, the run whose file sorts first wins and the other whole run is rejected. Rejecting both runs, or only the observations, is a decision for later.
- A carry-forward run is rejected when its original's run file is rejected for an unrelated reason, until the original is imported.
- Ticket-scope usage with no attempt on a carried-forward ticket is accepted and counted. The orchestrator may legitimately report its own usage that way, so this needs a policy decision.
- No new authz capability was added; a role check stands in for it.

DM-170 is done: an append-only metric observation ledger with stable ids, full attribution and provenance, exported and imported with the tracked run history. All four criteria are shown by rerunnable scripts under scratch/DM-170/ (128 PASS lines, ALL PASS in every script). Typecheck, oxlint on every changed file, and the 30 existing test files of the touched modules (760 tests) pass.

What was added:
- **Schema v10** (`src/core/db/migrations.ts`): table `metric_observations`.
  - One row per producer-chosen `mo_` id, with project, epic, run and (optional) sprint, ticket and attempt.
  - Each row keeps the `MetricObservation` fields from DM-169, plus cause, intervention, usage scope (`self`, `child`+`childRef`, `inclusive`), `carried_from`, the actor's role and label, `payload_hash` and `recorded_at`.
  - CHECKs: value is NULL exactly when the state is missing, and never negative.
  - A trigger refuses every UPDATE; only deleting the epic removes rows.
- **Contract** (`src/core/space/ledger.ts`): one set of rules shared by the service and the importer.
  - Strict draft and entry schemas built on DM-169's `metricObservation`, and an unkeyed `observationPayloadHash`.
  - `ledgerRuleViolation`: the attribution chain is complete, each scope and inherited scope is one of the observation's own, usage scope goes only with usage metrics, carry-forward goes only with cause `carry_forward`, and no machine-local id or label is carried.
  - Label checks: absolute, home and URL paths, `~user`, backslash-rooted paths, drive letters, UNC paths, `$HOME`/`%VAR%`, control characters, line separators, lone surrogates, any claim token (`maskClaimTokens`) and any `dmg_` grant token are refused.
  - Also `provenanceViolation`, `planAttributionViolation`, `isOriginalExecution`, `actorLabel` (clips the label, or falls back to the role), `usageTotal`, row mapping and insert.
  - Caps: at most 500 observations per call and 2,000 per run, so a run's history stays inside the importer's 8 MiB record limit.
- **Service** (`src/core/services/observations.ts`): `recordObservations`, all or none, and `listObservations`.
  - Readers are refused, the branch is checked, and the run must be owned by this machine.
  - The attempt must belong to the run; ticket and sprint are filled from the attempt and the plan it ran against, and must agree with it.
  - A human source needs the desktop session; this run's raw claim secrets are refused.
  - Carry-forward rules are enforced.
  - The same payload again returns `unchanged`; a changed payload returns `conflict`.
  - The run_history outbox entry is queued in the same transaction.
- **Run history** (`src/core/repo/portable.ts`): an optional `observations` key, absent when a run has none, so legacy bytes and hashes do not change.
  - Each entry is re-checked against the shared rules, provenance, its attempt and ticket, the carry-forward rules and the payload hash.
  - Duplicate ids are refused.
- **Importer** (`src/core/repo/importer.ts`): rejects a run file when an observation:
  - belongs to another project, or is already stored for another run or with another payload;
  - names a ticket or sprint outside the plan, or the wrong sprint for its ticket;
  - uses an id that another run file in the same import also lists;
  - has a carry-forward reference that does not resolve to an original execution stored here or imported with it.
  - Rows are inserted after attempts. A stored row that does not match fails that run's savepoint.
- **Other edits**:
  - `epicDeletion.ts` deletes observations first.
  - `src/test/repoEnv.ts` `dumpDomain` now includes the table.
  - `migrations.test.ts` expectations moved to v10, a deliberate change.
  - `docs/architecture.md` has a new ledger section and the persistence notes.

A reviewer should know:
- Nothing in `src` calls `recordObservations` yet. Producers belong to DM-171..176, so `npm run deadcode` will flag the new exports until then.
- No unit tests were written, per the epic policy.
- I kept the role check for readers rather than adding a new authz capability, to avoid changing a shared interface file.

outputs.summary:
DM-172 adds a pure, deterministic projection that turns timestamped lifecycle events and host activity spans into timing for attempts, tickets, sprints and runs. All four criteria are shown on five checked-in clock fixtures with hand-derived expected values, and through real services with the test clock. An adversarial reviewer found 20 defects. Seven are fixed and confirmed on its own probes, plus parts of two more; the rest are open and listed in notes.

What is built:
- Contract (src/shared/domain/timing.ts): each measure has a fixed `measure` key, `basis`, `unit: "ms"`, `state`, `valueMs` (null exactly when missing), `knownMs`, `unknownMs`, `coverage` and `open`. Time breakdowns always add up (active + waits + unknown = window). Wait classes: queue, blocked, build_test, review, human_approval, paused, idle. Anything not classified is `unknown`.
- Projection (src/core/space/timing.ts with timingFacts.ts, timingSpans.ts, intervals.ts):
  - Claim-to-submit is elapsed time only; active time comes only from host-reported spans. Verification and research count as active work, never waste.
  - Missing stops are bounded by later records, never invented. An expired or lapsed lease ends execution at the lease end shown by the grants in order; a grant after the lease ran out revives nothing; sign-in pauses hold leases.
  - Duplicate deliveries count once and arrival order changes nothing; overlap counts once.
  - Summed effort includes every attempt (rejected, failed, expired, canceled, superseded) and is separate from the wall-clock union. Orchestrator, reviewer and unattributed overhead stay in their own buckets, and are missing rather than 0 when nothing was reported.
  - Checkpoint waits count as human only when a person approved; other endings are unknown.
- Input boundary (src/core/space/timingInput.ts): a strict schema, and an adapter that reads the event log first and falls back to attempt and run records. A stop a record cannot date (`exact: false`, e.g. in an imported run) only bounds execution.
- Read-only run service: src/core/services/timing.ts `projectRunTiming`. Nothing calls it yet (DM-178 will).
- Docs: docs/space-grading.md (Timing section) and docs/architecture.md.

DM-175 attempt 2 fixes both review reasons on top of the attempt-1 commits; everything from attempt 1 is kept. I added two commits.

1. **A report that leaves out the origin no longer drops a confirmed escape (c2).** In `src/core/services/escapedDefects.ts`, `withAttribution` looks for a report that names no origin, no candidates, no sprint and no `unassign`. If its defect identity (case-insensitive) already has a report in the run, it stores the defect's current attribution with it: origin ticket and attempt, or candidates and sprint. The current attribution comes from the latest earlier report, in the same order the read model uses (`byRecorded`, now exported from performance.ts).
   - Reports are now recorded in call order, so a report in the same call also reads the ones before it.
   - A retried report reads only the reports recorded before its stored one, so it is still `unchanged` even after the defect moved later.
   - `origin: null` counts as naming no origin, so it does not drop the charge either.
   - Moving a defect to the run now needs a new explicit `unassign: true` input. It is refused with `invalid_input` when it also names an origin or candidates.
   - Review probe, case 3b (fix without origin): DM-1 and sprint 1 now show counted=1 with `fix-dropped:counted`. Before, both showed 0 and the defect was gone.
2. **No erasure without a trace (c2).** In `src/core/space/performance.ts`, `defectViews` now keeps a defect when any of its reports concerns the subject. When the latest report has moved it elsewhere (another ticket or sprint, or the run), it is listed uncounted with a new `DefectUncountedReason`, `reattributed`, added in `src/shared/domain/signals.ts`. Every report and who recorded it stay on the view. Withdrawn and duplicate reasons are checked first.
   - Review probe, cases 2b and 4b: the defects stay listed on DM-1 and sprint 1 as `withdrawn` and `duplicate`. Both already keep the origin through fix 1.
